Scientist Challenge

Bioprocessing has millions of possibilities than any one mind can hold.

While other disciplines received the gift of computation, a scientist is still disadvantaged by trial and error, experience, and heaps of data.

What is Trellis

From recommending the design of experiment (DOE), building protocols, ingesting the experimental data, to recommending the next design space, Trellis’ suite of bioprocessing toolbox helps you get to controllable bioprocess, and scale-up faster and with fewer runs.

Why Trellis

Lab-in-the-loop

We validate Trellis process recommendation in our own wet lab, using real-world feedback to fine-tune the tool.

Systems thinking

Trellis' data models reason from first principles across molecular, mesoscopic and macroscopic scales.

Adapts to the user

Trellis works as a guide to a new scientist, and acts like a peer to an experienced one.

Diligently Regulator ready

Case study

There really is a faster way to scale new heights

OFAT, DoE and Trellis were benchmarked on the same virtual 12-factor CHO fed-batch process. Trellis reached effectively the full known optimum; DoE plateaued near 77%, OFAT near 50%.

The difference is where the experiments go. OFAT searches locally, DoE spreads broadly and wastes runs far from the optimum, Trellis explores uncertain regions and concentrates where better performance is most likely.

% of known optimum reached on a simulated 12-factor CHO fed-batch process.

Science first, with AI as orchestration layer

Mechanistic at the core

Trellis combines scientific reasoning with machine learning. AI orchestrates a set of agents that build your models, and those models account for bioprocess mechanics that most dry-lab tools leave out.

The full design space, all at once

Trellis handles design spaces with up to 50 parameters and explores the entire space, with every parameter in play at the same time, until it gets you to the true global optima.

The fewest runs to get there

Tell Trellis your target response, your run budget and your setup. It selects the right sampling methodology and objective, then recommends the right DoE across the entire design space, so you run the least number of experiments.
